title: The Configurations Signature Database — Overview: the Signature setup philosophy
body: Signature edition. Original Signature-developed content; never mixed with public records. The Signature setup philosophy holds that a system should arrive already sensible: defaults chosen for the user, not for the vendor. Every default is a decision made on the user's behalf, and the doctrine requires each one to be defensible out loud. Configuration exists for the exceptions, not the rule — if everyone changes a setting, it was the wrong default. These are original doctrines, labeled as such.
capabilities: Configuration for exceptions, not the rule

title: The Configurations Signature Database — Signature defaults doctrine
body: Signature edition. Original Signature-developed content; never mixed with public records. The Signature defaults doctrine writes the default list as a contract: each default names the user it serves, the reason it was chosen, and the date it was last reviewed. Defaults expire — a default unreviewed for a year is a guess wearing a uniform. The demo audits a defaults list for expired entries.
capabilities: Defaults as a contract with named users
Reason and review date on every default
The uniform test for stale defaults

title: The Configurations Signature Database — Signature change doctrine
body: Signature edition. Original Signature-developed content; never mixed with public records. The Signature change doctrine makes every configuration change a small ceremony: state the intent, name the rollback, make the change, verify the intent held. Changes go in one at a time — never stacked, never rushed — because stacked changes hide which one broke things. The demo runs the ceremony checklist against a change record.
capabilities: Change as ceremony: intent, rollback, verify
One change at a time, never stacked
Verification of intent, not just absence of errors

title: The Configurations Signature Database — Signature secret doctrine
body: Signature edition. Original Signature-developed content; never mixed with public records. The Signature secret doctrine treats secrets as radioactive: smallest possible quantity, shortest possible half-life, handled with tongs. Secrets never appear in configs, logs, or screenshots; they arrive at runtime through narrow channels and are rotated on schedule, not after incidents. The demo scans a config for secret-shaped values and fails the build if any are found.
capabilities: Secrets as radioactive: minimal quantity, short half-life
Never in configs, logs, or screenshots
Rotation on schedule, not after incidents

title: The Configurations Signature Database — Signature recovery doctrine
body: Signature edition. Original Signature-developed content; never mixed with public records. The Signature recovery doctrine practices resurrection: every system must be rebuildable from its configuration records alone, by a competent stranger, without asking the original builders. Recovery drills are scheduled like fire drills — announced, timed, and reviewed — and the drill report names what was missing. The demo verifies a recovery bundle's completeness.
capabilities: Rebuildable from records alone, by a stranger
Recovery drills scheduled like fire drills
Drill reports name what was missing

title: The Configurations Signature Database — Signature naming doctrine
body: Signature edition. Original Signature-developed content; never mixed with public records. The Signature naming doctrine names every configuration thing like it will be read at 3 AM during an outage: full words, no clever abbreviations, environment in the name, purpose in the name. db-primary-prod is a name; db1 is a riddle. The demo grades names against the doctrine.
capabilities: Environment and purpose in the name

title: The Configurations Signature Database — Signature drift doctrine
body: Signature edition. Original Signature-developed content; never mixed with public records. The Signature drift doctrine assumes configurations wander: humans touch things, updates reset things, entropy edits things. So the doctrine watches — the declared configuration is compared against the live system on schedule, and every difference is either approved or reverted. Unexplained drift is treated as an intruder until proven otherwise. The demo detects drift between declared and live.
capabilities: Declared vs live compared on schedule

title: The Configurations Signature Database — Signature minimal doctrine
body: Signature edition. Original Signature-developed content; never mixed with public records. The Signature minimal doctrine keeps configurations small: every setting must earn its place by being different from the default or load-bearing for the system. Settings that match defaults are deleted; settings nobody understands are investigated, then deleted or documented. The demo prunes a config down to its load-bearing settings.

demo.title: Config pruner
demo.code: function prune(cfg,defaults){const o={};for(const k in cfg)if(cfg[k]!==defaults[k])o[k]=cfg[k];return o;}const p=prune({a:1,b:2,c:3},{a:1,b:9});J({kept:Object.keys(p)});assert(JSON.stringify(Object.keys(p))==='["b","c"]','prune');
